items.title: ReplaySSM: Rethinking State Storage for Faster Hybrid-Model Decoding
items.abstract: Hybrid models interleave state-space model (SSM) layers with a few attention layers. NVIDIA Nemotron 3, Qwen3.5 through Qwen3.8, Kimi-K3, and GLM-5.3-Flash are... Hybrid models interleave state-space model (SSM) layers with a few attention layers. NVIDIA Nemotron 3, Qwen3.5 through Qwen3.8, Kimi-K3, and GLM-5.3-Flash are all built this way, with Mamba-2, Gated DeltaNet (GDN), or Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) as the SSM layer. SSM layers are designed to make decoding fast: they use a fixed-size state in place of a key-value (KV) cache that grows with… Source
items.title_ko: NVIDIA, 하이브리드 모델용 ReplaySSM 공개 — SSM 상태 저장 방식 재설계로 디코딩 속도 개선
items.summary: ReplaySSM은 SSM 레이어와 소수의 어텐션 레이어를 섞은 하이브리드 모델을 위한 상태 저장 기법이다. NVIDIA Nemotron 3, Qwen3.5~3.8, Kimi-K3, GLM-5.3-Flash 등은 Mamba-2, Gated DeltaNet(GDN), Kimi Delta Attention(KDA) 같은 SSM 레이어를 사용해 디코딩을 빠르게 한다. SSM 레이어는 시퀀스 길이에 비례해 커지는 **KV 캐시 대신 고정 크기 상태**를 사용하도록 설계되어 있다. ReplaySSM은 이 고정 크기 상태의 저장 방식을 재고해 디코딩 효율을 높이는 접근을 다룬다.
items.why_it_matters: 긴 시퀀스를 다루는 하이브리드 아키텍처가 확산되는 가운데, 상태 저장 방식 개선은 추론 비용과 지연 시간에 직접 영향을 미쳐 실제 서비스 배포에 중요하다.
items.whats_different: 기존 어텐션 기반 모델의 KV 캐시가 시퀀스 길이에 따라 선형적으로 증가하는 것과 달리, SSM 레이어는 고정 크기 상태를 사용하며 ReplaySSM은 이 상태 저장 방식 자체를 재설계한다.

items.title: Self-Compacting Language Model Agents
items.abstract: Long agent traces composed of chains of thought and tool calls accumulate stale content that anchor subsequent generations, and eventually outgrow the context window. Existing scaffolds mitigate it with fixed-interval compaction triggered at a token threshold. Such triggers pay no heed to trajectory structure, risking discard of partial results mid-derivation or mid-search. We propose SELFCOMPACT, a scaffold that allows the model itself to decide when and how to compact. Specifically, it pairs two inference-time elements: (i) a compaction tool the model invokes to summarize the accumulated…
items.title_ko: Apple, 에이전트가 스스로 압축 시점 정하는 SELFCOMPACT 제안 — 고정 토큰 임계값 트리거 한계 보완
items.summary: 장시간 동작하는 에이전트는 사고 과정과 도구 호출 기록이 쌓이면서 오래된 내용이 이후 생성에 악영향을 주고 결국 컨텍스트 창을 초과하게 된다. 기존 방식은 고정된 토큰 임계값에 도달하면 압축을 트리거하는데, 이는 궤적 구조를 고려하지 않아 추론이나 탐색 도중에 부분 결과를 잘라낼 위험이 있다. 이에 저자들은 모델 스스로 언제, 어떻게 압축할지 결정하게 하는 스캐폴드인 **SELFCOMPACT**를 제안한다. 이는 모델이 호출해 누적된 내용을 요약하는 압축 도구를 포함한 두 가지 추론 시점 요소로 구성된다.
items.why_it_matters: 에이전트의 장기 작업 신뢰성은 컨텍스트 관리 방식에 크게 좌우되므로, 압축 시점을 모델이 자율적으로 판단하게 하는 접근은 긴 체인의 추론·도구 호출을 다루는 실제 에이전트 설계에 중요한 시사점을 준다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 고정 토큰 임계값 기반 압축 트리거와 달리, SELFCOMPACT는 궤적 구조를 고려해 모델이 직접 압축 시점과 방식을 결정한다.

items.title: Turning Opportunistic AI Inference Capacity Into Better Ads Recommendations
items.abstract: At Meta, we’ve built a system that enhances ads recommendations by leveraging idle inference capacity in our fleet. Two elasticity levers in the system allow ads recommendation work to expand across opportunistic capacity, without compromising baseline performance. This post describes how we designed and now operate the system at Meta’s scale and how it drives significant advertiser value and capacity efficiency. Inference fleets face a capacity paradox: They can be globally constrained while meaningful pockets of capacity remain locally idle. At Meta, we built a system that aggregates these pockets into a shared opportunistic capacity pool and turns them into better ads recommendations. By putting otherwise idle capacity to work, the system helps people see more relevant ads and improves advertiser outcomes without requiring additional capacity orders. Using this opportunistic capacity safely is difficult. It’s distributed across team-owned capacity allocations, regions, and accelerator types, and may be reclaimed with little notice. The ads inference system must therefore adapt workload as capacity supply changes without overloading the dedicated capacity that serves baseline workload. We address this challenge with two complementary elasticity levers. Rank More Ads (RMA) adjusts the number of candidates evaluated by the ranking stages. Serve Better Models (SBM) adjusts the share of requests routed to a more powerful model. Physical and logical isolation protects the capacity reserved for baseline serving. Separate feedback loops control RMA candidate volume and SBM model coverage, while value-aware load shedding at both servers and clients allows the system to degrade gracefully when capacity is suddenly reclaimed. Together, these mechanisms allow optional work to expand and contract with opportunistic capacity while protecting latency and reliability. The Inference Capacity Paradox: Globally Constrained, but Locally Idle Inference fleets must maintain enough capacity to meet demand under strict latency and reliability targets. However, demand and capacity rarely align perfectly across time, regions, resource combinations, and accelerator types. Capacity can therefore remain idle in parts of a fleet even when the fleet is constrained overall. Common causes include: Peak-provisioning and demand-variation mismatch: Inference fleets must be provisioned for peak demand, while traffic varies by time of day and season. Capacity needed during peak periods can therefore remain temporarily idle when demand is lower. Model-development and capacity-delivery timing mismatch: Inference capacity arrives on supply-chain timelines, whereas models are developed and launched on separate schedules. This creates a gap between when capacity becomes available and when models are ready to consume it. Regional resource-ratio mismatch: Inference workloads require accelerators as well as supporting resources such as CPUs. When these resources are not available in the required proportions, one resource can remain idle while another limits serving capacity. Accelerator-type mismatch: Inference fleets can span multiple accelerator vendors, generations, and architectures. Workloads are not always portable across these accelerator types, which can strand capacity on hardware that cannot immediately serve the available demand. These mismatches create an industry-wide inference capacity paradox: A fleet can be globally constrained while meaningful pockets of capacity remain locally idle. At Meta’s scale, these temporary pockets can collectively represent substantial capacity and create better ads recommendations when used safely. From Fragmented Reservations to a Shared Opportunistic Capacity Pool Across a heterogeneous fleet at Meta’s scale, instantaneous idle inference capacity is inevitable — even with proactive planning designed to minimize structural mismatches. items.title_ko: Meta, 유휴 추론 용량으로 광고 추천 고도화 — RMA·SBM 탄력성 레버로 베이스라인 성능 유지
items.summary: Meta는 유휴 상태의 추론 용량을 광고 추천 작업에 활용하는 시스템을 구축했다. 분산된 유휴 용량 조각들을 하나의 **공유 기회 용량 풀**로 모아 베이스라인 성능을 해치지 않으면서 추가 작업을 수행하게 한다. 핵심은 두 가지 탄력성 레버로, Rank More Ads(RMA)는 랭킹 단계에서 평가하는 후보 수를 늘리고, Serve Better Models(SBM)는 더 강력한 모델로 라우팅되는 요청 비율을 조정한다. 물리적·논리적 격리로 베이스라인 서빙용 용량을 보호하며, 용량이 갑자기 회수될 때 서버·클라이언트 양쪽에서 가치 기반 로드 셰딩으로 점진적으로 작업을 축소한다.
items.why_it_matters: 추론 인프라는 전체적으로는 용량이 빠듯해도 지역·시간대·가속기 종류에 따라 국지적으로 유휴 자원이 남는 '용량 역설'을 겪는데, 이를 활용하면 **추가 하드웨어 투자 없이** 광고 추천 품질과 광고주 성과를 개선할 수 있다는 점에서 대규모 추론 인프라 운영 전반에 시사점이 크다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 고정된 팀별·리전별 용량 할당 방식과 달리, 유휴 용량을 공유 풀로 통합하고 RMA·SBM 두 레버와 로드 셰딩으로 안전하게 가변 활용한다는 점이 차별점이다.

items.title: Can we change an AI model’s architecture without retraining it from scratch?
items.abstract: AI agents are rapidly scaling: longer sessions, deeper reasoning chains, more autonomy. But the Transformer architecture underneath them still pays a memory tax that grows with the number of tokens it processes. As agents become more capable, that cost scales with them. Now, there’s a proliferation of hybrid architectures that use some combination of methods to achieve a better balance of memory, speed, and quality. Those methods include sparse attention, which selects a subset of past tokens to consider when selecting the next token; sliding-window attention, which preserves only the most recent tokens; and state space models, which compress information from the full history into a fixed-size state. These hybrid architectures can be understood as points in a sequence-model design space: to differing degrees, they mix information while traversing a sequence and passing through different states. What distinguishes them from each other is how they retain and use the past. Until now, exploring this design space has required training every new architecture from scratch, using trillions of tokens and hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours. This has made controlled comparisons of hybrid architectures extremely expensive. In a new paper, “Priming: Hybrid state space models from pre-trained Transformers,” our team at Amazon Web Services addresses this problem. We introduce priming, a method that leverages pretrained Transformer weights as a starting point to reduce the pretraining cost of hybrid architectures by more than 99%. With priming, model developers can ask questions that were previously too expensive to answer at scale: Which attention layers can be replaced by more-efficient layers? How many attention layers can be replaced without sacrificing quality? Which state space layer works best? And what does the trade-off between speed and accuracy look like? In our paper, we compare hybrid models that use three different types of state space models (Gated KalmaNet, Gated DeltaNet, and Mamba-2). Some of our findings: Not all state space models are equal. Under controlled conditions, Gated KalmaNet (GKA) performs best, followed by Gated DeltaNet (GDN) and then Mamba-2. GKA uniquely offers variable-length inference computation without retraining and gives the user direct control over its position on the speed-accuracy frontier. A good lossy summary of everything beats a perfect recording of the most recent past. State space models consistently outperform sliding-window attention (SWA), even when SWA gets twice the memory budget. Same quality, twice the throughput. A 32-billion-parameter GKA-based hybrid model matches its source Transformer on reasoning benchmarks while decoding up to twice as quickly with 128,000 tokens of context and reaching correct answers in as little as two-thirds of the wall-clock time. To foster further research on hybrid architectures, we have released a zoo of primed hybrid models at the eight-billion-parameter and 32-billion-parameter scales for long-context reasoning and instruction following, together with training code, optimized kernels, and a vLLM-serving plugin under the Apache 2.0 License. The attention mechanism A Transformer’s attention mechanism — which determines how relevant previously seen tokens are to the token currently being processed — relies on three different vectors, which take their names from database design: the query, the key, and the value. For each token, the query captures what that token is “looking for,” the key captures what it “offers,” and the value carries the actual information it will pass along. Relevance is computed by comparing the current token’s query against every other token’s key; the closer the match, the more that token’s value contributes to the output of attention. Each of these vectors is produced by multiplying the token by a learned weight projection matrix. items.title_ko: Amazon, 'Priming' 공개 — 사전학습 Transformer 재활용해 하이브리드 아키텍처 학습비용 99% 절감
items.summary: Amazon Web Services 팀이 사전학습된 Transformer 가중치를 출발점으로 삼아 하이브리드 상태공간 모델(SSM)을 만드는 **Priming** 기법을 제안했다. 이를 통해 하이브리드 아키텍처의 사전학습 비용을 99% 이상 줄여, 어떤 어텐션 레이어를 어떤 SSM으로 교체할지 대규모로 실험할 수 있게 됐다. Gated KalmaNet, Gated DeltaNet, Mamba-2 세 가지 SSM을 비교한 결과 Gated KalmaNet이 가장 우수했고, SSM들은 동일 품질에서 슬라이딩 윈도우 어텐션보다 2배 높은 처리량을 보였다. 320억 파라미터 GKA 기반 하이브리드 모델은 원본 Transformer와 동등한 추론 성능을 유지하면서 12만8천 토큰 컨텍스트에서 최대 2배 빠르게 디코딩하고, 정답 도달 시간을 3분의 2까지 단축했다.
items.why_it_matters: 에이전트형 AI가 길어진 세션과 깊은 추론 체인을 다루면서 Transformer의 메모리 비용이 커지는 문제가 심화되는데, 이를 해결할 하이브리드 아키텍처 탐색을 **대규모 재학습 없이** 저비용으로 가능하게 한다는 점이 중요하다.
items.whats_different: 기존에는 새로운 하이브리드 아키텍처마다 수조 토큰과 수십만 GPU-시간을 들여 처음부터 재학습해야 했지만, Priming은 사전학습된 Transformer 가중치를 재사용함으로써 이 비용을 99% 이상 줄였다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Minions: A Dynamic and Distributed Virtual GPU Cloud Built on Idle Apple Silicon Devices
items.abstract: The increasing demand for GPU-accelerated machine learning inference has exposed limitations in centralized GPU infrastructures, including high cost, limited elasticity, and long wait times under resource constraints. At the same time, modern Apple Silicon–based macOS devices are equipped with powerful GPUs that remain largely idle during normal usage. This paper presents Minions, a dynamic and distributed virtual GPU cloud that aggregates idle Apple Silicon GPUs across macOS devices to execute large-scale machine learning inference workloads. Minions enables teams to leverage existing…
items.title_ko: Apple, 유휴 Apple Silicon GPU 모아 가상 GPU 클라우드 'Minions' 공개 — 대규모 추론 워크로드 분산 처리
items.summary: Minions는 macOS 기기에 탑재된 Apple Silicon GPU 중 평소 사용되지 않는 유휴 자원을 모아 대규모 머신러닝 추론 워크로드를 실행하는 동적 분산 가상 GPU 클라우드다. 기존 중앙집중형 GPU 인프라는 비용이 높고 탄력성이 부족하며 자원이 제한될 때 대기 시간이 길어지는 문제가 있다는 점에서 출발했다. Minions는 여러 macOS 기기에 흩어진 GPU를 집계해 팀이 기존 유휴 하드웨어를 활용할 수 있도록 지원한다.
items.why_it_matters: GPU 수급난 속에서 **유휴 Apple Silicon GPU**를 추론 인프라로 재활용할 수 있다면 중앙 GPU 클라우드 의존도를 낮추고 비용을 절감할 수 있다.
items.whats_different: 기존 중앙집중형 GPU 클라우드 대비, 이미 보유한 macOS 기기의 유휴 GPU를 분산 집계해 활용한다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Simulating student learning for better AI tutoring
items.abstract: At a glance StudentSim is a research system for evaluating and improving AI tutors before they are tested with real learners; it is not a product, is not deployed in classrooms, and is not intended to replace teachers AI tutoring tools need feedback from students to improve, but collecting that feedback through human studies is slow, costly, and difficult to scale StudentSim trains personalized AI student simulators from publicly available, de-identified learner records, with one simulator adapted to each student The work evaluates simulators along two education-grounded dimensions: whether they respond like a specific student, and whether they update after tutor guidance Across chess, second-language English writing, and mathematics, StudentSim outperforms leading baselines and provides a useful feedback signal for training an AI tutor In research settings, teams are exploring how AI-powered tutoring systems can help explain a math problem, suggest an edit to a writing assignment, or guide a learner through a chess position. Yet the quality of teaching cannot be measured only from the tutor’s answer. A tutor needs to know what happens after the guidance reaches a student. Did the student correct the original mistake? Did the hint help them reason toward the answer, or did it give away too much? Would a different student need a different kind of support? In today’s AI tutor research, answering these questions often requires real learner studies. Those studies are valuable, but they are slow and costly to run, which makes it hard to use student feedback during fast model iteration. StudentSim is an AI system that creates personalized simulators of individual students, modeling how they answer questions and how their answers change after receiving a tutor’s guidance. The goal is to make student feedback more available during AI tutor development. This research also introduces StudentSimEval, a benchmark and evaluation protocol spanning chess, second-language English writing, and mathematics. Importantly, the goal is not to replace teachers or classroom learning. Instead, StudentSim helps researchers evaluate and improve AI tutoring systems during the research and development process before testing them with real learners. The research uses only publicly available learner datasets released for research use with de-identified records; no personally identifying information is used at any stage. Figure 1: AI tutors need feedback from students to improve. Student simulators can approximate part of that feedback during research-stage training and evaluation. They provide an early-stage research signal, not a replacement for testing with real learners. Measuring what a student simulator needs to do A simple way to build a student simulator is to ask a large language model to role-play a learner. For example, a prompt might say, “You are an elementary-school student who struggles with math.” The model can change its tone and express uncertainty. The harder part is preserving the learner’s actual ability boundary. A model may speak in a young student’s voice while still relying on knowledge and reasoning far beyond that student’s level. For training an AI tutor, this can produce misleading feedback: the tutor may appear effective because the simulated student is too capable. Traditional student modeling approaches face a different limitation. Knowledge tracing and behavior prediction models are grounded in real learning records and can estimate a student’s current knowledge, skills, and learning habits. Many of these models, however, were not designed to take natural-language tutor guidance as input. They can help describe what a student has done, but they do not always tell us how a student would respond to a particular explanation, hint, or Socratic question. items.title_ko: MS, 학생 시뮬레이터 StudentSim 공개 — 체스·영작문·수학서 기존 AI 튜터 베이스라인 능가
items.summary: StudentSim은 공개된 비식별 학습자 기록을 바탕으로 개별 학생을 모사하는 AI 시뮬레이터로, AI 튜터를 실제 학습자 대상 테스트 전에 연구 단계에서 평가·개선하기 위한 시스템이다. 각 시뮬레이터는 특정 학생처럼 응답하는지, 그리고 튜터의 안내 이후 답변이 실제로 업데이트되는지라는 두 가지 교육학적 기준으로 평가된다. 체스, 제2언어로서의 영어 글쓰기, 수학 세 영역에 걸쳐 **StudentSim은 기존 베이스라인을 능가**했으며, AI 튜터 학습에 유용한 피드백 신호를 제공했다. 이와 함께 StudentSimEval이라는 벤치마크 및 평가 프로토콜도 함께 공개됐다.
items.why_it_matters: 실제 학습자를 대상으로 한 피드백 수집은 느리고 비용이 많이 들어 AI 튜터의 빠른 모델 반복 개선을 어렵게 만드는데, **시뮬레이션 기반 피드백**은 이를 연구 단계에서 보완할 수 있는 수단이 된다.
items.whats_different: 단순히 LLM에 '수학을 어려워하는 초등학생' 역할을 맡기는 방식은 말투는 흉내 내지만 실제 학습자의 능력 한계를 벗어난 과도하게 유능한 답변을 내놓아 튜터 평가를 왜곡시키는 반면, 또한 **기존 지식 추적(knowledge tracing) 모델**은 실제 학습 기록에 기반하지만 자연어 형태의 튜터 안내를 입력으로 받아 반응을 예측하도록 설계되지 않았다는 한계가 있다.

items.title: Deploy decision models with llama.cpp on Amazon SageMaker AI
items.abstract: Applications that route requests, select agent actions, or assign policy outcomes often need scores over a fixed set of choices instead of free-form text. Deploying these decision models with llama.cpp on Amazon SageMaker AI gives you a managed path for serving quantized models on CPU or GPU infrastructure. This post continues a series on specialized AWS Deep Learning Containers (DLCs) for generative AI inference. Previous posts cover WhisperX , vLLM-Omni – Part 1 , and vLLM-Omni – Part 2 . In this post, you first use the AWS DLC for llama.cpp to serve OpenAI-compatible chat completions through SageMaker AI InvokeEndpoint . You then extend the same runtime with SemIf , formerly OpenJev, which returns probabilities over declared options without decoding an answer token. The accompanying code sample includes CPU and GPU deployment options. Solution overview Figure 1 shows two deployment paths from the same packaged model. The text-generation path uses the AWS DLC for llama.cpp and returns generated responses through the OpenAI-compatible API. The structured-decision path builds a child image that replaces the default server with a SemIf adapter and returns probabilities for declared options. Figure 1: Run the AWS DLC for llama.cpp or the SemIf child image on CPU or GPU, depending on the API and latency requirements of your workload For the standard path, package the model as model.tar.gz in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) and reference the published DLC image directly. The container finds the first .gguf file under /opt/ml/model , maps POST /invocations to llama-server at /v1/chat/completions , and passes SM_LLAMA_CPP_* environment variables to llama.cpp arguments. The llama-server HTTP API doesn’t expose the final-position logits and state operations that SemIf uses. The structured-decision path therefore uses AWS CodeBuild to build a child image and store it in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) . The child image keeps the DLC’s compiled CPU or CUDA libraries while replacing its entry point with a SageMaker-compatible adapter. Understand the input and output schemas The AWS DLC for llama.cpp accepts the OpenAI Chat Completions schema. Send a messages array with role and content , plus generation controls such as max_tokens and stream : { "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "A customer cannot receive a password reset email. Reply with the best support queue." } ], "max_tokens": 64, "stream": false } The response uses the OpenAI-compatible choices array. Read generated text from choices[0].message.content . SemIf uses a constrained decision schema instead of chat messages. The request contains a caller-defined ID, unstructured state, a question, and an ordered list of allowed options: { "decision": { "id": "support-route", "state": "The customer cannot receive a password reset email.", "question": "Which queue should handle this request?", "options": [ {"id": "account_access", "description": "Account access support."}, {"id": "billing", "description": "Billing support."} ] } } The response returns option_ids , probabilities , and raw option_logits in the same order, along with prompt, timing, and pinned model metadata. With stable option IDs, your application can apply thresholds, fallbacks, and policy checks without parsing generated prose. SemIf belongs to a broader class of decision models that score application-defined outcomes from unstructured state. Other implementations include Jev , TypeSafe’s decision model and /v1/systemone API; Kev , a model server designed for TypeSafe API compatibility; and Strands Decider 2B , a purpose-built model for agent workflows with calibrated outputs. Choose the right decision workflows Use this pattern when your application defines the allowed choices at request time and needs a model to interpret unstructured context. Examples include routing a case to a queue, extracting one value from a known set, assigning an incident priority, checking a policy outcome, o
items.title_ko: AWS, llama.cpp로 SageMaker에 '결정 모델' 배포 — SemIf 어댑터로 옵션별 확률 반환
items.summary: 이 글은 AWS DLC의 llama.cpp를 Amazon SageMaker AI에 배포해 라우팅, 에이전트 행동 선택, 정책 결과 할당 같은 작업에 필요한 '선택지 점수' 기반 결정 모델을 서빙하는 방법을 다룬다. 기본 경로는 OpenAI 호환 Chat Completions API로 텍스트를 생성하지만, **SemIf**(구 OpenJev)라는 확장 어댑터를 적용하면 답변 토큰을 디코딩하지 않고 정의된 옵션들에 대한 확률을 직접 반환한다. SemIf는 llama-server HTTP API가 노출하지 않는 최종 위치 로짓과 상태 연산을 활용하기 위해 AWS CodeBuild로 별도의 child 이미지를 빌드해 ECR에 저장한다. 요청은 caller가 정의한 ID, 비정형 상태, 질문, 허용 옵션 목록으로 구성되며, 응답은 option_ids, probabilities, raw option_logits를 순서대로 반환한다.
items.why_it_matters: 자유형 텍스트 생성 대신 고정된 선택지에 대한 확률을 얻으면 애플리케이션이 생성된 문장을 파싱하지 않고도 **임계값, 폴백, 정책 검증**을 바로 적용할 수 있어 운영 신뢰성이 높아진다. CPU/GPU 양쪽에서 양자화 모델을 관리형으로 서빙할 수 있다는 점도 비용·지연 최적화 측면에서 실무적으로 유용하다.
items.whats_different: 기존 llama-server의 OpenAI 호환 채팅 완성 API 대비, SemIf는 답변 토큰 디코딩 없이 안정적인 옵션 ID와 확률·로짓을 직접 반환하는 제약된 결정 스키마를 사용한다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: ARCS: Towards Precise Text-to-SQL via Structured Disambiguation
items.abstract: As text-to-SQL systems move beyond demonstrations toward real-world deployment, ambiguity in user questions becomes a primary source of errors. Such ambiguities are often subtle, domain- or data-specific, and can silently cause system outputs to deviate from the user's true intent. Ambiguity is traditionally addressed through conversational clarification, which is often inefficient, cognitively demanding, and poorly aligned with real-world user workflows. We propose structured disambiguation, a new paradigm in which ambiguity is resolved through explicit, constrained interactions rather than free-form dialogue. We construct ARCS (Ambiguity Resolution Corpus for SQL), the first text-to-SQL benchmark featuring naturally occurring, unconstrained ambiguities over real-world databases, with complete annotations of all valid ambiguity points, interpretations, and SQL queries. Experimental results show that text-to-SQL remains challenging in the presence of ambiguity: gpt-6-sol achieves only 51% end-to-end execution accuracy, and no open-source model exceeds 27%.
items.title_ko: ARCS 벤치마크 공개 — 모호한 질문 포함 Text-to-SQL, gpt-6-sol도 정확도 51%에 그쳐
items.summary: 텍스트-투-SQL 시스템이 실제 환경에 배포될수록 사용자 질문의 모호성이 주요 오류 원인이 되고 있다. 기존에는 대화형 명확화로 이를 해결했지만 비효율적이고 사용자 워크플로우와 맞지 않는 문제가 있었다. 이 논문은 자유 대화 대신 명시적이고 제한된 상호작용으로 모호성을 해소하는 '구조화된 명확화' 패러다임을 제안한다. 실제 데이터베이스에서 자연 발생한 모호성을 모든 해석과 SQL 쿼리까지 완전히 주석 처리한 최초의 벤치마크 ARCS를 구축했다. 실험 결과 모호성이 있는 상황에서 **gpt-6-sol도 실행 정확도 51%**에 그쳤고, 오픈소스 모델은 모두 27%를 넘지 못했다.
items.why_it_matters: 모호성 처리는 text-to-SQL의 실제 배포 성패를 가르는 핵심 요소인데, 최상위 모델조차 절반 수준의 정확도에 머문다는 점은 현 시스템의 한계를 명확히 보여준다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 대화형 명확화 방식 대신, 명시적이고 제약된 상호작용으로 모호성을 해소하는 구조화된 명확화 패러다임을 제시한 점이 다르다.

items.title: Clinician use of language models diverges from how the models are evaluated
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) assistants are being deployed to clinicians across health systems, and judgments about their readiness rest largely on benchmark scores, most of them derived from examination questions or curated cases. A benchmark predicts performance in deployment only to the extent that its items resemble real use, yet whether benchmarks reflect the work these systems receive has rarely been measured. Here we analyze 127,833 queries sent by 6,342 physicians, advanced practice providers and nurses in 35 specialties to an institutional assistant during an eight-month roll-out. We characterize each query with RCQ-Map, a clinician-validated framework grounded in taxonomies of clinical questions and of LLM evaluation, which records its task, intent, answerability, missing information and potential harm. Documentation and administration (36.2%) and knowledge retrieval (28.9%) made up nearly two-thirds of use, and diagnosis 3.7%; more than a third of queries could not be answered well as posed. Applying RCQ-Map to 58 public benchmarks drawn from major evaluation suites and frontier model reports, which we assemble into the Clinical AI Benchmark Atlas, showed that the median benchmark contained no documentation requests and shared 31% of the task mix of real use, less than an even spread across task categories would. Benchmarks in suites designed to resemble clinical practice were individually no closer to real use than those used in frontier model reports. Benchmark scores therefore say little about how clinical AI performs on most of the work it is actually given, and evaluation should be matched to real clinical use.
items.title_ko: 의료현장 LLM 사용 12만 쿼리 분석 — 기존 벤치마크, 실제 업무와 31%만 일치
items.summary: 8개월간 35개 전문분야 임상의 6,342명이 보낸 127,833건의 LLM 질의를 분석한 연구다. 연구진은 임상의 검증을 거친 RCQ-Map 프레임워크로 각 쿼리의 과제, 의도, 답변 가능성, 누락 정보, 잠재적 위해를 분류했다. 실제 사용의 36.2%는 문서화·행정 업무, 28.9%는 지식 검색이었고 진단은 3.7%에 불과했으며, 쿼리의 3분의 1 이상은 제대로 답변하기 어려운 형태였다. 58개 공개 벤치마크를 같은 방식으로 분석한 결과(Clinical AI Benchmark Atlas), 중간값 벤치마크는 문서화 요청을 전혀 포함하지 않았고 실제 업무와의 과제 구성 **일치율은 31%**에 그쳤다.
items.why_it_matters: 임상 특화를 표방한 벤치마크 스위트조차 프런티어 모델 보고서용 벤치마크와 실제 업무 유사도에서 차이가 없어, 벤치마크 점수가 실제 임상 배치 성능을 예측하지 못할 수 있음을 시사한다.
items.whats_different: 기존 벤치마크들은 시험 문제나 선별된 사례 중심으로 구성되는데, 이 연구는 실제 127,833건의 현장 쿼리 분포와 비교해 **벤치마크-실사용 간 괴리**를 정량적으로 측정했다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: uber/causalml v0.18.0
items.abstract: This release **deprecates positional `treatment` and `y`** ahead of the v1.0 switch to `fit(X, y, treatment, ...)`, makes **causal trees and forests estimate leaves honestly by default**, and moves the **uplift trees and forests onto the shared Cython tree kernel**, with native missing-value support. It also adds benchmark dataset loaders with ground-truth metrics, new CATE evaluation scores, model `save()` / `load()`, and a rebuilt [documentation site](https://causalml.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) with an end-to-end tutorial, an estimator guide and an FAQ. The full notes, with measurements, are in the [changelog](https://causalml.readthedocs.io/en/stable/changelog.html). ## ⚠️ Breaking Changes * **`BaseSLearner.estimate_ate` always returns `(ate, lb, ub)` and no longer accepts `return_ci`.** `ate = learner.estimate_ate(...)` now binds a tuple, and passing `return_ci` raises `TypeError`; unpack instead: `ate, lb, ub = learner.estimate_ate(...)`. By @su-jin1425 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1031 ## Deprecations * **Positional `treatment` and `y` emit a `FutureWarning` (#854).** In v1.0 the positional order becomes `fit(X, y, treatment, ...)`, the scikit-learn convention. Pass both by keyword — `learner.fit(X=X, treatment=treatment, y=y)` — which is correct before and after the flip. A call left positional will silently train on swapped arguments at v1.0 rather than raise. See the [migration guide](https://causalml.readthedocs.io/en/stable/migration.html). By @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/975 ## Behavior Changes These change fitted models or estimates without any edit to your code. * **`CausalTreeRegressor` and `CausalRandomForestRegressor` default to `honesty=True`**: the tree structure is grown on one half of the sample and leaf values are re-estimated on the other ([Athey & Imbens 2016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.01132)). Pass `honesty=False` for the previous behavior. By @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1001 * **The default propensity models produce different scores**: log-loss model selection over a wider `C` grid for the logistic models, `max_depth=3` (was 8) for `GradientBoostedPropensityModel`, and a seeded, stratified early-stopping split. By @arpitjain099 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/944, @su-jin1425 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1033 and @ismailvc1111 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1051 * **`UpliftTreeClassifier` and `UpliftRandomForestClassifier` run on the shared tree kernel.** Names, arguments and output shapes are kept; `X_val` / `treatment_val` / `y_val` and `early_stopping_eval_diff_scale` are ignored with a `UserWarning` (use `prune_fraction` instead), and `DecisionTree` is deprecated. By @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/973 * **`UpliftRandomForestClassifier` defaults to `n_jobs=None`** (was `-1`), because peak memory grew with the core count. Predictions are unchanged; pass `n_jobs=-1` to restore. By @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/992 * **`causalml.features.load_data` returns `numpy.ndarray` instead of `numpy.matrix`**, and no longer raises when the one-hot encoder produces no columns. By @arpitjain099 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/978 and https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/979 ## New Features * Benchmark dataset loaders (`fetch_lalonde`, `fetch_ihdp`, `fetch_twins`), ground-truth metrics (`pehe`, `ate_error`, `policy_risk`) and a reproducible leaderboard notebook by @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1015 * `ccp_alpha="cv"` on the causal tree: cost-complexity pruning with the tree size chosen by cross-validation by @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1001 * `pretrain=True` on `CausalTreeRegressor.estimate_ate` and `BaseDRIVLearner.estimate_ate` by @jeongyoonlee in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1024 * `prune_fraction` on `UpliftTreeClassifier` for validation-based pruning inside `fit` by @jeongyoonlee in https://githu
items.title_ko: uber/causalml v0.18.0 공개 — CausalTree에 honesty 기본 적용, uplift 트리 Cython 커널로 통합
items.summary: causalml v0.18.0은 v1.0 전환을 앞두고 fit() 인자 순서를 변경하며 **positional treatment/y 사용 시 FutureWarning**을 발생시킨다. CausalTreeRegressor와 CausalRandomForestRegressor는 기본값으로 **honesty=True**가 적용되어, 표본 절반으로 트리 구조를 만들고 나머지 절반으로 리프 값을 재추정한다. UpliftTreeClassifier와 UpliftRandomForestClassifier는 공유 Cython 트리 커널로 이전되어 결측값을 네이티브로 지원하며, 이름과 출력 형태는 유지된다. 이 외에 lalonde, ihdp, twins 등 벤치마크 데이터 로더와 pehe, ate_error, policy_risk 같은 ground-truth 평가 지표, 모델 save()/load(), 재구축된 문서 사이트가 추가됐다.
items.why_it_matters: causal forest 및 uplift 모델링 결과가 기본 동작 변경(honesty, propensity 모델 스코어 등)으로 달라질 수 있어, 기존 파이프라인의 재현성을 점검해야 한다.
items.whats_different: 기존 CausalTreeRegressor의 비honest 추정 방식 대비 **Athey & Imbens(2016)**의 honesty 기법을 기본값으로 채택했고, UpliftTree는 별도 구현 대신 causal tree와 동일한 Cython 커널을 공유하도록 통합됐다.
